scope: Six independently constructed relic artwork proposals. Existing effects, titles, localization and flavor remain unchanged. Runtime PNGs and active selection manifests are frozen for the independent ATC package.

nativeReferences.principles: Bold silhouette, a few large color planes, thick irregular dark contour, controlled values; construction and negative space give identity. No native icon is copied into an output, and new generations have no reference-image inputs.

export: Generated original pixels copied unchanged only into the separate drafts folder. Contact sheets proportionally resize the entire image canvas, retaining native optical margins; native48/32 samples are actual pixel sizes, not magnified.
acceptance: Author visual inspection and local artifact review only. No human visual approval, technical runtime acceptance, engine/build/test/install or live UI is implied. Runtime transfer requires a separately coordinated K6 asset window.

assets.title: The Relic Remover
assets.concept: Ivory ratchet claw pries open an empty relic collar.
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. One ORIGINAL Slay the Spire2-style inventory RELIC ICON for La Rata Remix, NOT a card illustration or scene. Genuine transparent background (alpha), square canvas ideally1254x1254. One complete centered object occupies75% canvas height with generous clean transparent margin. Match the visual economy of native Anchor/Vajra/MembershipCard: thick dark charcoal irregular outline, few broad hand-painted flat planes, only2–3 values per material, slight organic asymmetry, bold silhouette readable at32px and48px. This must be an unusual specific tangible relic with a little story, not a generic UI symbol. Restrained palette, no realism, glossy3D, fine engraving, ornamental filigree, tiny accessories, particle effects, scenery, backdrop, drop-shadow rectangle, letters, numbers, text, labels, icon border or watermark. Distinctive CONSTRUCTION rather than extra decoration.

DESIGN: A strange pocket-sized RELIC UNFASTENER made from TWO OVERSIZED CURVED IVORY MOLARS hinged together like a squat lobster claw. A single broad dark CORAL-RED ratchet joint connects them. The two blunt hooked tooth-jaws wedge apart one EMPTY antique-brass collar/socket ring, opening it into a clear C-shaped gap. Design as one coherent handheld contraption, no hand. The open collar is visibly detached/unfastened, not destroyed by a sword. Main silhouette is a compact asymmetrical ivory pincer around an empty round brass socket, with the red hinge as a strong third shape. Few forms, no extra gears or bolts. Story: an old tooth-puller repurposed to remove cursed treasure, leaving its valuable mounting behind. NOT a generic crowbar, scissors, hammer or wrench. Palette bone cream, coral-red hinge, muted brass, dark contours.

Readable removal/tool silhouette; no complex mechanism or scattered debris.

DESIGN: An admission TICKET that has folded itself into a tiny PAPER FERRY BOAT. A wide shallow angular cream-paper hull with a large black scorched stern; its two pointed bow/stern tips curve back toward each other in a clear return-shaped silhouette. One chunky burnt-orange folded interior plane resembles a surviving ember. One large ROUND PUNCHED HOLE in the raised ticket flap makes the origin as a used ticket legible, no printed markings. The whole object is one charred folded paper ticket-boat, not a full ship, no mast, oar or water. Broad ivory triangle planes against soot-black outer edge, muted rust orange interior. Story: a burned passage ticket became its own boat to bring something back from the discard shore. NOT an ordinary flat rectangular ticket with decorated corners, not a scroll, flame icon or generic origami crane. Keep max5large paper planes.

DESIGN: A bizarre ancient KEY fabricated from a miniature staircase bent into one solid stepped object. The main shaft is a bold three-step DESCENDING ZIGZAG of dark brick-red cast iron, with three broad ivory worn tread surfaces. Its upper end has a thick rectangular arch shaped like an EMPTY TINY DOORWAY, not a circular key bow. Lowest step ends in one stout sideways key tooth. The entire key silhouette is a squat descending staircase with a doorway at its high end, tilted modestly diagonally. Clearly three big descending treads, no extra tiny steps or rails. Material heavy red iron and worn pale stone integrated as one relic. Story: someone folded an entire secret stairway until it would fit in a lock. NOT a standard gold key with stair-shaped teeth pasted on. No gold filigree, gems, sparks or background.

DESIGN: One lopsided cast-bronze MOCKING BELL whose mouth is stretched sideways into a broad rude laughing opening. A broad thick PLUM-PURPLE TONGUE hangs in one curved hook out of its dark interior, and the tongue's tip IS A SECOND SMALL UPSIDE-DOWN BELL rather than a standard round clapper. DESIGN: A peculiar bottle STOPPER that is a sleeping SILVER MOON-FISH. The fish's thick body curls into an asymmetric crescent, with one tiny simple closed-eye slash, no scales. Its single wide folded tail is wedged down into a SHORT BROKEN VIOLET GLASS BOTTLENECK COLLAR, physically sealing it. No cork at all: the moon-fish itself is the plug. One large turquoise potion-drop bead rests in the crescent belly opening, captured like a stored possibility. The neck is only a chunky short collar, not an entire bottle. Main silhouette a curled ivory/silver fish, broad forked tail below and jagged violet glass collar; cold silver/navy/violet with one turquoise bead. Story: the bottle is gone but its moon-shaped keeper still holds one impossible drop. Organic handmade ceramic/silver object, no detailed fins/scales, no stars or glow cloud. NOT a generic crescent stuck on top of a brown cork. Max4large shapes.
